summary.oneLiner: IKS delivered 18.5% YoY revenue growth and 39% PAT growth by scaling its AI-native platform while reducing headcount, with strategic wins in mid-sized health systems and a land-and-expand model for large systems; the pending TruBridge acquisition positions it to dominate rural healthcare with integrated EHR+AI, creating a unique data moat and cross-market synergy.

one-line thesis: IKS delivered 18.5% YoY revenue growth and 39% PAT growth by scaling its AI-native platform while reducing headcount, with strategic wins in mid-sized health systems and a land-and-expand model for large systems; the pending TruBridge acquisition positions it to dominate rural healthcare with integrated EHR+AI, creating a unique data moat and cross-market synergy.
financial scorecard: revenue: +18.5% YoY (INR857cr Q4), +20% FY26 (INR3,193cr); EBITDA/margin: +33% YoY to INR300cr (35% margin) Q4, +38% FY26 to INR1,091cr (34% margin); PAT (rptd): +39% YoY to INR206cr Q4, +48% FY26 to INR721cr; PAT (normalized): excludes TruBridge due diligence costs (INR38cr Q4) and debt write-off (Q3), normalized PAT growth ~35% YoY; order book: not disclosed; net debt: reduced from INR850cr peak to INR251cr as of Mar 2026
guidance: revenue growth: implied >15% YoY for FY27 based on momentum; margin: EBITDA margin to stabilize near 34-35%; order inflow: expected to accelerate with TruBridge close and AQuity cross-sell; capex/commissioning: minimal capex; TruBridge integration to drive $162B rural market entry
segment / subsidiary detail: Top 10 customers: INR452cr (53% of Q4 revenue), grew 28% YoY; Top 5: grew 18% YoY; 90% revenue from repeat clients; 450+ large enterprise clients; AQuity cross-sell: 1 full-platform win (Holyoke), 1 expansion (Mission Community), 1 land-and-expand win (top 5 health system in RCM/value-based care); AI features: Scribble Select (multi-variant scribing), MyCare Hub (multi-agent patient engagement), autonomous coding in 2 specialties, integrated with Epic
growth verticals / optionality: TruBridge acquisition (rural healthcare EHR+AI platform); Certilytics partnership (payer-provider collaboration to reduce denials); MyCare Hub expansion into predictive resource optimization (ICU, OR, nurse utilization); SLMs built for rural care applicable to physician groups
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 35% Q4 (from 34% FY25) despite INR38cr one-off TruBridge due diligence costs; cost leverage from 5.3% headcount growth vs 18.5% revenue growth; offshore model fully integrated from AQuity; FX hedge loss (INR12cr) partially offset by forex gain (INR35cr), net benefit INR23cr
capex / expansion: minimal; focus on R&D and AI model training; no major capex disclosed; TruBridge integration will require tech integration spend, not disclosed
capital allocation: debt reduction: net debt down to INR251cr from INR850cr peak; M&A: TruBridge acquisition pending (expected close FY27); share buybacks or dividends: not mentioned; R&D: significant investment in AI engineering (550 FTEs), ThinkDTM acquihire, Certilytics partnership
risks & watch-items: TruBridge regulatory approvals pending; large health systems slow to adopt full platform; payer API access limitations for collaboration; AI hallucination risks in clinical workflows; currency volatility (FX gain/loss impact); integration risk of TruBridge EHR into IKS platform
management quality / tone: highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; emphasized AI-native transformation as core moat; proud of operational leverage (revenue up 18.5%, headcount up 5.3%); optimistic on TruBridge synergy and rural market; transparent about AQuity GTM missteps and pivot; tone is founder-led, tech-obsessed, and outcome-driven
non-obvious takeaways: 1) 45% female workforce including 5 C-suite leaders is a strategic differentiator in a male-dominated tech-health space; 2) Scribble Select’s multi-variant design (autonomous + human-in-loop) is a rare industry-first that solves adoption plateau (50-60% usage → likely >80%); 3) TruBridge’s 15M+ patient data is the real moat, not AI — enables longitudinal labeled datasets for superior SLMs; 4) Rural outpatient care models (70% of TruBridge volume) directly transferable to IKS’s core physician group market

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims to be "The only Comprehensive platform that delegates all chores across the patient journey", spanning Pre-visit, Peri-visit, In between visits and Post-visit stages of the patient journey.
- Addresses a stated TAM of US$260bn with an Outsourced Market of US$34bn (CY2023), growing at 8% / 12% CAGR respectively (2023-2028E), against US Healthcare Expenditure of US$5tn (CY2024); TAM is defined as "Total Addressable Market for RCM, VBC, Patient, Coding and Client Services" per a Zinnov Report.
- Established client relationships: "85%+ Revenues from Repeat Customers" and "5+ Years" average vintage for Top 10 / Top 5 clients (as of Mar 31, 2026); repeat clients are defined as those who availed the platform in the previous period.
- Serves "600+/650+ Healthcare Organizations" (Q1 27/Q1 26) and "450+ Enterprise level customers"; note the deck's organisation count is lower in Q1 27 than Q1 26 without explanation.
- Strategy is framed as "5 strategic pillars of execution", covering a proprietary-model System of Action for the large medical group market, integrated SOA & System of Record (SOR) for the rural/community health system market, re-stratified growth levers, margin recovery via operating model transformation and synergies, and culture and leadership.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] TruBridge RCM & Coding Businesses appear as an owned unit requiring "Operating model Transformation", and its rural/community installed base is a named cross-sell target; the deck repeatedly cites "one-time acquisition costs" affecting Q1 FY27 margins but does not state the acquisition's price or terms.
- [Associate/Investment] The deck refers to "increased equity base from revaluation of Abridge" as a reason ROE declined, and reports a "Share of Profit/(Loss) from Associates (net of tax)" line, indicating an associate/minority holding that is not otherwise described.
- [Awards] AMGA Distinguished Corporate Partner Award 2026; Best CFO & Finance Strategy Excellence Awards 2026 for Excellence in Investor Relations (organisational) and Best CFO in Healthcare for Nithya Balasubramanian, Whole-time Director & Group CFO; 2026 Dallas-Fort Worth Titan 100 for Sachin K. Gupta, Founder & Global CEO.
- [Track record] "A decade of consistent profitable growth" with a stated 28.7% Revenue CAGR and 46.4% PAT CAGR; the deck does not state the exact period these CAGRs span.
- [Geography] Business is US-facing (US healthcare expenditure TAM, US clients, USD revenue reporting) while the registered office and workforce base are in India; revenue grew 20.7% YoY in INR against 12.0% in USD, indicating material currency translation effect.
